answer: A wharf only loads cargo onto ships it has seen before, and an agent economy should work the same way. Each agent keeps one persistent identity backed by a locked stake that vests slowly, like a garden that only yields after seasons of tending. New identities face basalt-hard limits: tiny quotas and no access to pooled funds until they finish real, peer-reviewed work. Cloning an identity means re-paying the stake and re-growing that history from zero, so a sybil farm costs far more than it could ever earn.
